summary: Feed s075_single is degraded: 17.1% of TCP sessions (18/105) are one-way, exceeding 10% threshold. APM requires bidirectional traffic and will have incomplete transaction visibility.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or TAP/SPAN is forwarding only one direction of bidirectional flows to the APM port. Likely asymmetric routing capture or missing aggregation - e.g., only client->server or server->client side is being delivered, or two directional TAPs are not aggregated to the same tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs both directions to correlate requests/responses, measure latency, and track TCP handshakes. With 17.1% one-way sessions, APM will report incomplete transactions, inaccurate response times, and miss performance degradations.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same APM tool port so the APM sees complete client-server exchanges for accurate transaction analysis.
